text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Prime Minister Tiit Vaehi said he had no intention of resigning over the alleged appartment privatisation affair, in which he is accused of illegally gaining ownership of former state property.
- The government will not meet demands by students to restore subsisides for public transport.
- Finance ministry officials had no insider information when they bought the Union Bank shares, the ministry's chancellor said.
- MP Arvo Junti was expelled from the Development Party after he announced his intention to leave the party's parliament faction.
- City mayor payroll figures approved by local councils of 8,000 to 15,000 kroons are close to the salary levels of government ministers.
- On avearge some 100 crimes per day have been registered in Estonia last year, with every other crime committed in Tallinn, police statistics shows.
- ERA Bank and Foreks Pank have launched a house loan project today, which can be covered by privatisation vouchers.
- Workers of the bankrupt Oru Peat factory, some of which were hunger-striking recently over unpaid wages, will be paid part of their wages on January 29, the company's administrator said.
- The formerly state-owned 13 buildings of the Tartu University will become university property, the government decided.
